sections.title: What the controllers do, as found
lines: For L1, Downstairs radiators, the fitted curve gives supply 34.1 C at 0 C outdoor, slope -0.69 C per C, and summer stop above 17.2 C.
For L2, Upstairs floor heating, the fitted curve gives supply 38.0 C at 0 C outdoor, slope -0.96 C per C, and summer stop above 22.4 C.
On L1 the direct heating share is 0.943 for fireplace and 0.057 for tv, so fireplace responds much more strongly in this measure.
For L2 kitchen, the held-out prediction error is 0.648 C on weeks the fit never saw.
The data could not separate the TV room's evening warming from people in it; that belief is not supported by the room data alone.
These findings are from logged data and simulation only; no controller change or building test is claimed.

sections.title: How sure we are
lines: The held-out error is 0.329 degrees C for fireplace and 0.276 degrees C for tv on L1, and 0.648 degrees C for kitchen on L2; this is the prediction error of room temperature on weeks the fit never saw.
The margin over no control is a model-comparison score of 13.6 for L1 and 43.6 for L2, where over 10 is strong and this is not energy and not degrees.
The spot readings changed the error versus other panel readings from 9.52 degrees C at 0 readings used to 5.35 at 1, 3.48 at 2, 1.94 at 3, and 1.97 at 4.

The operator belief that L2 is the same curve as L1 with a flat reduction is refuted: the gap widens as it gets colder; L2 runs its own curve, and the belief that the TV room warms on evenings from the people in it is not supported by the room data alone.

Site context programs for L1 and L2 were all worse than the blind best, for example 39.2 for Curve value; Max limit; Min limit on L1 and 26.16 for Two heating circuits, L1 and L2, one outdoor sensor on L2, where positive delta_bic_vs_blind_best means worse than the best program found without site context and over 2 is a real difference.

sections.title: What the data cannot tell yet
lines: The outdoor data only covers -1.6 °C to 28.8 °C, so the data cannot tell how the controller behaves outside that range.
The curve fit reports a supply level and a slope for each loop, but the logged data cannot tell whether the level or the slope is the part that matters; it only shows the fitted curve.
The belief that L2 is the same curve as L1 with a flat reduction is refuted: the gap widens as it gets colder.
The belief that the TV room warms on evenings from the people in it is not supported by the room data alone.

The site-context programs are not supported: all are worse than the blind best, with delta_bic_vs_blind_best 39.2 for Curve value; Max limit; Min limit on L1, 25.93 for Autumn drying on L1, 19.36 for Outdoor temperature delay on L1, 34.74 for Max limit on L1, 15.56 for Min limit on L1, 26.16 for two heating circuits on L2, and 34.61 for the floor heating plus warm air program on L2; positive means worse than the best program found without site context and over 2 is a real difference.

sections.title: Next observation
lines: The next observation is a fresh Home Assistant pull covering the heating season since the last pull. It would settle whether the fitted curves still describe the rooms over that longer logged period.

sections.title: Yhteenveto huoltomiehelle (suomeksi)
lines: Ohjain ajaa kahta piiriä: L1 on alakerran patterit ja L2 on yläkerran lattialämmitys.
L1:n käyrä antaa menoveden 34.1 °C, kun ulkona on 0 °C, käyrän jyrkkyys on -0.69 °C per °C ja kesäpysäytys on yli 17.2 °C.
L2:n käyrä antaa menoveden 38.0 °C, kun ulkona on 0 °C, jyrkkyys on -0.96 °C per °C ja kesäpysäytys on yli 22.4 °C.
Kylmien viikkojen datassa L1:lle paras malli oli 'S0 No control (free-floating)' ja seuraavan mallin delta-BIC-ero oli 5.88, joten L1:n ohjauksen hyötyä ei voi vahvistaa tästä datasta.
L2:n keittiön ennustevirhe näkemättömillä viikoilla oli 0.648 °C, ja paneelilukemien sovitevirhe oli 3.48 °C kahdella lukemalla ja 1.94 °C kolmella lukemalla.
Lue paneelilta seuraavaksi tuore Home Assistant -haku, joka kattaa viime haun jälkeisen lämmityskauden.

glossary.delta_bic_curve_over_no_control: model-comparison score: how much better the curve explains the room data than no control, after a complexity penalty. Over 10 is strong. NOT energy, NOT degrees.
glossary.held_out_error_c: prediction error of room temperature on weeks the fit never saw, degrees C
glossary.heating_share_by_room: each room's share of the loop's direct heating coupling, 0 to 1
glossary.error_vs_other_panel_readings_c: how far the fitted curve is from panel supply readings not used in the fit, degrees C
glossary.controller_sensor_minus_fmi_c: controller's own outdoor sensor minus the weather station, degrees C
glossary.delta_bic_vs_blind_best: positive = worse than the best program found without site context; over 2 is a real difference
glossary.next_observation: the cheapest next check, already chosen by the system - report it, do not invent another
